steps.title: Weigh in air
steps.instruction: Hang the sinker on the spring balance and read its weight.

steps.title: Fill the overflow can
steps.instruction: Fill the can until water runs out of the spout, and wait until it stops dripping.

steps.title: Place the cylinder
steps.instruction: Put an empty measuring cylinder under the spout.

steps.title: Lower the sinker
steps.instruction: Lower the sinker until it is completely under water, without touching the bottom.

steps.title: Read the cylinder
steps.instruction: Read the volume of water that overflowed.

steps.title: Compare
steps.instruction: Enter the upthrust (loss of weight) and the weight of the water displaced.

air-2.text: Let it hang still before reading.

air-3.text: Record the reading with the sinker in air.

can-1.text: Any water that runs out now must not be counted later.

can-2.text: Fill past the spout, then wait for the last drip.

can-3.text: Fill the can, then press Wait until the dripping stops.

cyl-1.text: Displaced water comes out of the spout.

cyl-2.text: Put the empty cylinder under it now.

imm-1.text: All of it must be under water.

imm-3.text: Lower until fully covered, clear of the bottom.

wat-1.text: It should read less than in air.

wat-2.text: Wait for the overflow to finish.

vol-1.text: Read the bottom of the meniscus.

cmp-1.text: Upthrust = weight in air − weight in water.

cmp-2.text: 1 mL of water has a mass of 1 g.

cmp-3.text: Weight of water = (volume in mL ÷ 1000) × 9.81 N.

observations.whatHappened: The sinker weighed less in water. The loss of weight was the same as the weight of the water it pushed out of the can.
observations.why: Water pushes up on anything in it. Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of the fluid displaced. A brass sinker displaces its own volume of water (20 mL = 20 g), so it is pushed up with about 0.2 N.
realWorld: Ships float because they displace a lot of water
Submarines take in water to sink

prompts.question: The upthrust on a fully submerged object depends on…
choices: its volume and the fluid's density
prompts.explain: Upthrust = weight of the fluid displaced = ρ V g.

prompts.question: Why wait for the can to stop dripping first?
choices: So only water pushed out by the sinker is collected
Water must settle to read the balance
prompts.explain: Otherwise the cylinder catches extra water and the volume is too big.

captions.text: Fill the can to the spout and wait for the last drip.
Lower it until fully covered, hanging freely.
Loss of weight equals the weight of water displaced.
